clauses.reason: Section 1(a) blocks, subject to the IEEPA section 203(b) exceptions and to regulations, orders, directives and licenses, all property and interests in property of the persons described in its sub-items that are in or come within the United States or the possession or control of United States persons. This inventory item is the opening of that lead-in. Current-law support selected as the predicate: 22 U.S.C. 9202(1)(A) (U.S. Code release point 119-121), a current statute that defines applicable Executive order to include Executive Order 13382, relating to blocking property of weapons of mass destruction proliferators and their supporters. It is read as consistent with the clause continuing, not as quoting the clause; the predicate is original_plus_bounded_search with this record added. The order rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12938 of November 14, 1994 (as amended by Executive Orders 13094 and 13382). The held presidential continuation notices selected in the packet run from 2011-11-09 to 2025-11-05 (14 notices, each naming the order by number); the latest, the notice of 2025-11-05 (90 FR 50737; FR Doc. 2025-19831), continues the emergency beyond November 14, 2025, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14. No held instrument revokes, supersedes, suspends or amends this clause, and the order contains no sunset, expiry or own-terms end.

Identity and text: the held original is the Federal Register text (70 FR 38567 (Federal Register, July 1, 2005)) of Executive Order 13382 of June 28, 2005, Blocking Property of Weapons of Mass Destruction Proliferators and Their Supporters. I read the held text in full; its title, number, date and Federal Register pages agree with the register row and the packet. The held text is the Federal Register text; its operative text and inventory were read in full. The clause inventory has 22 clauses and matches the text I read. Status YES is retained on the established original_plus_bounded_search route: the held original; no own-terms end (the order has no sunset, expiry or self-revocation); every held later instrument that names the order is either attached as a later event or explained in the earlier-end check as not acting on it; the national-emergency predicate; and the three bounded searches. Emergency predicate: The order rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12938 of November 14, 1994 (as amended by Executive Orders 13094 and 13382). The held presidential continuation notices selected in the packet run from 2011-11-09 to 2025-11-05 (14 notices, each naming the order by number); the latest, the notice of 2025-11-05 (90 FR 50737; FR Doc. 2025-19831), continues the emergency beyond November 14, 2025, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14. The packet's selectable notices omit the years 2014 between the first and last held year; I do not rely on those years, and the latest notice itself continues an existing emergency. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes in the packet: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, statute text and editorial notes, edition current through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML, 49 titles read) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes, 6942 catalog records, plus operative sentences in 16784 saved order texts). Each is marked complete with no coverage warning; they are machine leads, and I read the held later texts myself. Cut-off: every clause is decided as of 2026-10-14. The Federal Register text of the order was read from the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF held at the original path; I confirmed identity from the heading, number, date and FR pages, not from page images.
